Build only this feature on this page. Get it working, test it, and then move on.

What you are building

Update one field inside the chosen JSON object and prove the saved completed state survives refresh. You are rebuilding the same feature with JSON storage, so keep the user experience aligned while the persistence model changes.

The key idea for this feature is Record updates, persistence, and visible status evidence.. Before you write anything, make sure you can describe what the user should see or what the request should do when this feature is finished.

Key words and definitions

TermMeaning
UpdateChanging an existing stored record.
Status fieldThe value that shows whether work is complete.
PersistenceA change that stays after refresh.
UI feedbackVisible evidence that the new state was applied.

Why this still matters to the client

  • Managers need a persistent completed state, not a temporary visual trick.
  • This page shows how one field inside one object can be updated and saved back to disk reliably.

What to carry in from earlier pages

  • Bring forward the success criterion about reliable status changes.
  • Reuse the same UI expectation from the SQL completion feature.

State-change habit

  • A style change in the DOM is not enough.
  • The backend must store the new status.
  • Refreshing the page is the simplest proof that the update persisted.

Completion state preview

A good completion feature changes both the stored data and the visible status.

Prepare report completed Saved

How this feature moves through the stack

HTMLJavaScriptFlaskStorageResponse

Useful reference before you code

  • A status change is only complete when the stored value and the visible state both update.
  • The design should make completed work readable without making the interface noisy.
  • Use this feature to reinforce the idea that UI state should reflect stored data.

Generic update-request pattern

fetch(`/api/items/${id}`, {
  method: "PATCH",
  headers: {
    "Content-Type": "application/json"
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({ status: "complete" })
});
PATCH

PATCH is used when you are changing part of an existing record.

status

Send only the value the backend actually needs to update.

JSON body

Even a small update still needs the data packaged clearly.

persistence

A true update survives refresh because the stored data changed, not just the styling.

Build it in this order

The completed state should be changed in the stored object first, then reflected back to the user.

Step 1 static/js/app.js

Send the update request from the correct task row

  • Use the stable task id rather than rebuilding the status in the DOM manually.
  • Keep the user action obvious: complete this one task.
Step 2 app.py

Find the matching object and change only the status

  • Load the task list, loop until you find the correct object, update the status field, then save the file again.
  • Check that no unrelated properties are being changed by accident.

Ask yourself

  • How do you know only one object changed?
  • Why is reloading the page a good proof of persistence?

Where the checks happen

HTML

The interface can require fields, constrain control types, and guide the user before submit.

JavaScript

The browser can check presence, shape, and request timing before sending data.

Flask

The backend must re-check the request because outside tools can bypass the browser entirely.

JSON write step

The document write logic must reject or repair bad structures before saving.

Where your work goes

File or areaWhy this file mattersWhat belongs in this feature
static/js/app.jsSends the update request from the list rowUse the stable task id and refresh after success
app.pyFinds the chosen object and updates its statusChange only the intended field, then save
data/tasks.jsonStores the changed objectThe saved status should match the visible status after refresh

When this feature is ready to sign off

  • The correct record changes to completed.
  • The completed state is visible in the UI.
  • Refreshing proves the change was saved, not just styled.
